problem: Production pricing controls appeared present in automated proof but user clicks did not reliably change visible pricing state, and selecting English on an unprefixed public page left the experience Dutch.
root_cause: Production proof asserted HTML marker presence rather than functional interaction state. Pricing visibility relied on semantic hidden state without an explicit runtime display fallback, while the public language selector redirected unprefixed pages to /en/* and therefore coupled switching to localized-route reachability.
prevention: Interactive production controls require state-change evidence, not marker-presence evidence alone.
Pricing lifecycle, plan-group and billing controls must be clicked in a production browser proof and the resulting visible state must be asserted.
Public-site language selection must use prebuilt static localized routes; runtime translation may be fallback capability but not the primary switching dependency.
Localized /en/* and /nl/* public routes require explicit routing coverage and production navigation proof.
A production English-switch proof must verify html lang=en, visible English copy, absence of the Dutch pricing H1, and absence of the runtime translation failure message.
Runtime/cache version changes require co-changing exact-version regressions in the same candidate.
No LIVE_BEWEZEN claim is valid for an interaction defect without browser-level production evidence of that exact interaction.
Never use a localized wildcard rewrite that also matches its own rewritten target. Generated locale files use Netlify pretty URLs directly; only locale-root mappings may be explicit.

evidence.observed_live_failure: Production /prijzen exposed 'Switching language failed. Try again.' after selecting English.
evidence.localized_route_failure: Live /en/prijzen returned an internal error after deploy 6ab4cad23bc6d5000871db3d; root cause was recursive wildcard rewrite.

failed_approaches: Treating presence of data-bg-* markers as proof that clicks changed user-visible state.
Relying on general route/browser health without an interaction-specific production assertion.
Using runtime translation as the primary public-site language-switch path, allowing provider failure to leave Dutch copy visible.
Adding /en/* -> /en/:splat.html and /nl/* -> /nl/:splat.html rewrites; the wildcard also matched the rewritten .html target and caused a recursive Netlify rewrite loop.
